# Aetheria — Full Site Passport for AI Agents and Bots

> Version 1.0 · Last verified 2026-10-22 · Canonical: https://hnylytskyi.dev
>
> This document describes the public Aetheria site end to end: both view modes, every persistent screen and state, all published content, all controls, the 3D world, the visual language, and a deterministic protocol for visual evaluation. It is written for AI assistants, crawlers, QA bots and human reviewers. Facts are taken from the source files listed in §10; features that exist only as unused code are marked as such instead of being presented as visible behaviour.

---

## 0. How to use this file

- **Text-only crawler:** read §3 (classic resume). It is the server-rendered, crawlable surface and contains all professional content. The 3D world is a WebGL canvas and cannot be read as text.
- **Browser-capable agent:** read §2 for URLs, §4 for the 3D world and §7 for the QA bridge. The bridge allows deterministic teleporting, camera placement and time-of-day changes.
- **Visual reviewer:** follow §8. Do not judge the 3D scene from this text; capture rendered frames.
- **Fact-checking:** each claim maps to a source file in §10. Where in-game dialogue disagrees with profile data, §9 says which source is authoritative.

## 2. Site model, URLs and persistence

### 2.1 One route, two modes

The whole site is a single Next.js App Router page at `/`.

- **Classic resume** is the default mode. It is a client component but its initial HTML is server-rendered, so crawlers without JavaScript can read the complete CV text. The page opens in this mode on first visit.
- **3D outpost** is a lazy-loaded chunk (`ssr: false`). It mounts only after the visitor chooses it or the URL asks for it. Entering 3D never reloads the page; language, theme and dossier live in the shared store, while classic-only UI state such as scroll position and the project filter is not preserved.
- On desktop (viewport width ≥ 900 px) the classic → 3D transition plays a short “warp” animation over the singularity background. On smaller screens the switch is immediate.
- Opening `?mode=3d` directly still serves the classic HTML first; after hydration the app switches to 3D. A visual test should wait for the 3D canvas and loader to settle.

### 2.2 URL parameters

| Parameter | Values | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `classic` or `3d` | Forces the view mode |
| `lang` | `en` or `uk` | Forces the language; wins over the stored preference and is written back to the URL |
| `q` | `low`, `medium`, `high` | Forces the 3D quality tier at canvas mount |
| `debug` | any presence | Enables the QA bridge and the physics wireframe overlay (`window.__aetheriaDebug`, `window.__aetheria`) |
| `probe` | any presence | Enables the renderer probe only (`window.__aetheria`) |

Two hash groups exist. The mode-selecting group forces the classic view and scrolls to the section: `#resume`, `#classic`, `#projects`, `#about`, `#education`, `#skills`, `#certifications`, `#contacts`. The section-anchor group exists for in-page navigation but is not in the mode-selecting list: `#hero`, `#interactive-3d`, `#resume-main`.

Examples:

- `https://hnylytskyi.dev/?mode=classic&lang=en`
- `https://hnylytskyi.dev/?mode=3d&q=high`
- `https://hnylytskyi.dev/?mode=3d&q=high&debug&lang=en`
- `https://hnylytskyi.dev/?lang=uk#skills`

### 2.3 State stored in the browser

| Key | Storage | Written when | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aetheria_theme` | localStorage | Theme changes | `light` or `dark`; also read by the pre-paint script |
| `aetheria_lang` | localStorage | Language changes | `en` or `uk` |
| `aetheria_time_of_day` | localStorage | Time-of-day slider moves | Cycle position `0..0.999` |
| `aetheria_intro_seen` | localStorage | Intro ends or is skipped | `1` = do not auto-play the cinematic intro again |
| `aetheria_dossier` | localStorage | Crew met / material opened | JSON `{ metCrew: string[], openedMaterials: string[] }` |
| `aetheria_bio_typed` | sessionStorage | Hero bio finishes typing | `1` = skip the typewriter for the rest of the session |

There are no cookies, no analytics, no tracking pixels and no backend API for visitor data.

### 2.4 Defaults

- Language: English.
- View mode: classic.
- Theme: OS preference on first paint; otherwise light. If the OS is dark on a first visit, the day/night cycle starts at midnight; otherwise at noon.
- Audio: muted.
- Dossier: empty.
- Quality tier: detected from GPU, CPU cores, memory and handheld signals; `?q=` overrides it.

## 3. Classic resume — complete map

### 3.1 Global chrome

**Background layers**

- A WebGL gravitational-singularity / quasar background with an infalling particle vortex. It reacts subtly to scroll velocity and is mounted on all devices, with particle count and DPR capped by quality tier.
- A CSS sky tint and a hero ambient aura driven by the shared day/night engine.
- The classic view uses the same time-of-day state as the 3D world; changing it in one mode is reflected in the other.

**Header (desktop)**

- Brand: `DH.` monogram plus the full name and the caption “Digital portfolio”.
- Primary navigation: Work, About, Education, Skills, Certificates, Contact.
- Time-of-day slider with moon and sun cap buttons; the track previews the sky gradient and the label shows the current period.
- Fallback theme button, shown where the slider is hidden (≤ 640 px).
- Audio toggle.
- EN / UA language switch.
- `3D` button that enters the 3D world.
- Thin scroll-progress bar at the bottom edge of the header.

**Header (mobile)**

- Brand, audio, language, 3D button and a horizontally scrollable section navigation below the header.
- The time-of-day slider is replaced by a binary theme button at ≤ 640 px.

**Other chrome**

- “Skip to content” link as the first focusable element.
- Back-to-top button appears after scrolling.
- Toast messages confirm email copy success or failure.

### 3.2 Sections 01–08

The page is numbered like an editorial document.

#### 01 — Hero

Shown:

- Availability pill with the status “Open to Remote Opportunities”.
- Live Kyiv clock (`Europe/Kyiv`).
- Eyebrow: “01 / Ideas. Code. Experience.”
- Name, role, and a rotating specialty line: 3D World Builder, WebGL Performance, Rapier Physics, Full-Stack Engineer, TypeScript Craftsman.
- A terminal-style typed bio (skipped for reduced motion or repeat visits in the same session).
- Primary CTA “Explore my work” → `#projects`; secondary CTA “Let's collaborate” → `#contacts`.
- Meta row: location, “Download PDF” (opens the print dialog), GitHub.
- Stats: `04` projects to explore, `04` technology disciplines, `07` certifications.
- “Scroll to discover” cue.
- A kinetic “ORBITAL ATELIER” artifact: a 3D-looking cube with nine orbit planes and moving satellites, a pause/resume button, and three links: “From idea to product” → `#projects`, “Architecture & technology” → `#skills`, “Step into the 3D world” → enters 3D.

#### 02 — Projects (“Selected Work”)

Shown:

- Section heading and subtitle “Real-world full-stack & 3D engineering applications”.
- Toolbar: “Showing N / 4” and, when a filter is active, the selected skill and a “Clear filter” button.
- Four project cards in a sticky scroll scene. Each card has:
  - A browser-chrome frame with a live-demo screenshot.
  - An “Explore project” overlay.
  - Clickable technology tags that filter the list.
  - Tagline, title, description, three of the four feature bullets.
  - Actions: Live Demo (when the project has a URL), Source Code, Project Details.
- With a fine pointer and motion allowed, the project image tilts slightly and a specular light follows the cursor.
- If no project matches the selected skill, an empty state appears with “Show all projects”.

#### 03 — About

- Heading “About Me” and subtitle “Engineering philosophy, architecture, and core focus”.
- Four numbered highlight cards, each with an icon and one paragraph from the profile summary.

#### 04 — Education

- Heading “Education & Academic Background”.
- One card: KPI, Institute of Atomic and Thermal Energy (IATE), specialty 121 “Software Engineering”, Bachelor's degree, 2023–2027, 4th year in progress, Kyiv.

#### 05 — Skills

- Heading “Tech Stack & Skills”, subtitle “Technologies and tools I use on a daily basis”.
- Instruction: “Choose a technology to discover the projects built with it.”
- Four category cards: Frontend Core & State; 3D & Creative WebGL; Backend & Databases; DevOps & Architecture.
- Every skill is a button; clicking it filters the projects section and scrolls to it.

#### 06 — Certifications

- Heading “Verified Certifications”.
- Seven cards: issuer, level, title, category, and a “Verified” link to the public credential.
- All seven are marked verified in the data.

#### 07 — Interactive 3D showcase

- Eyebrow “Interactive Experience”.
- Technology badges: Three.js, React Three Fiber, Rapier Physics, GLSL Shaders.
- Headline “Want to experience this stack live?”.
- Description of the 3D world.
- Primary CTA “Launch 3D Experience” (desktop: warp transition; mobile: direct).
- Decorative holographic compass ring.

#### 08 — Contacts

- Eyebrow “The next chapter”.
- Availability pill.
- Headline “Have a project in mind?” and the collaboration paragraph.
- Primary button with the email address (mailto).
- “Copy Email” button with a success toast and a check icon.
- Three contact links: Email, Telegram (“Start a conversation”), GitHub (“Explore the code”).

#### Recognition

- A footer-adjacent “Recognition” block with the official Web Guru Awards “Guru of the Day” badge image.
- Text: Aetheria was selected on 8 October 2026.
- Link “View the award”.
- The badge is embedded in the page flow, not as a fixed overlay.

#### Footer

- `DH.` brand link back to the top.
- Copyright with the current year and the author's name.
- “See you in 3D” button.

### 3.3 Classic actions

| Action | Where | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Navigate sections | Header / mobile nav / footer | Smooth scroll to the section; active section is highlighted |
| Filter by skill | Skills cards or project tags | Projects list filters; toolbar shows `N / 4`; scrolls to projects |
| Clear filter | Projects toolbar or empty state | Restores all four projects |
| Explore project | Project image / “Project Details” | Opens the project modal (also reachable from 3D) |
| Live Demo | Project card / project modal | Opens the sibling project site in a new tab |
| Source Code | Project card / project modal | Opens the GitHub subtree in a new tab |
| Change time of day | Header slider, moon/sun cap | Animates the sky and switches the DOM theme at thresholds |
| Toggle theme | Fallback button (small screens) | Animates the cycle to the opposite pole |
| Toggle audio | Header | Enables/disables ambient audio and UI cues |
| Switch language | Header EN/UA | Instantly re-renders all copy; updates `<html lang>` and the URL |
| Download PDF | Hero meta row | Opens the browser print dialog with the print-only CV document |
| Copy email | Hero/contacts | Writes the email to the clipboard and shows a toast |
| Email / Telegram / GitHub | Contacts | Opens the corresponding link |
| Enter 3D | Header, hero artifact, section 07, footer | Switches to the 3D world, optionally after the warp |
| Back to top | Floating button after scroll | Scrolls to the hero |
| Pause artifact | Orbital artifact button | Stops/resumes the cube animation |

### 3.4 Project modal

The same modal is used from the classic page and from the 3D world. It contains:

- A macOS-style browser frame with the project screenshot and its URL.
- Tagline and title.
- Description.
- “Key Highlights” — all four feature bullets.
- Tech stack tags.
- Footer actions: Live Demo (if the project has a public URL) and Source Code.
- Close by button, backdrop click or `Escape`; focus is trapped inside.

Projects with a public demo: Forma-3D, TerraScope, Lumina. Aetheria itself has no external Live Demo URL and shows Source Code only.

### 3.5 Print document

“Download PDF” calls `window.print()`. A dedicated print-only document is rendered for the browser's print preview:

- Header with name, role, location, email, Telegram, GitHub and website.
- Professional Summary (bio plus the four summary bullets).
- Core Technical Skills (four categories, inline).
- Featured Projects (all four, with stack, description and feature bullets).
- Education.
- Verified Certifications (all seven).
- Footer with name, email, Telegram and website.

The visitor chooses “Save as PDF” in the browser dialog. The site does not generate or download a PDF file directly.

### 3.6 Visual behaviour and accessibility

- Display font: Space Grotesk (self-hosted via `next/font`); body text uses the system UI stack.
- Design language: editorial monochrome, thin borders, glass panels, large radii (26 px), numbered sections, generous whitespace, warm accent colour derived from the current sky.
- The page supports light and dark themes through CSS custom properties on `<html data-theme>`.
- Focus-visible outlines are provided; the skip link is the first tab stop; modals trap focus and close on `Escape`.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` disables the typed bio, the rotating specialty, the intro flight, project tilt and other decorative motion.
- Section reveal animations are used on scroll but content is present in the DOM.

#### Projects

**1. Forma-3D (Space Base Scene Editor)**

- Tagline: Modular 3D Space Base scene editor & outpost configurator.

  1. Optimistic UI and instant client state caching via TanStack Query v5.
  2. Role-based access (Student / Teacher) with JWT rotation and rate limiting.
  3. Interactive lesson media player supporting video, PDF, Google Drive, and Cloudinary CDN.
  4. Visual student progress curves and study schedules powered by Recharts.

**4. Aetheria (Interactive 3D WebGL Portfolio & Hub)**

- Tagline: Interactive 3D outpost & developer portfolio hub.
- Description: Comprehensive interactive 3D WebGL portfolio built with Next.js 15, Three.js, React Three Fiber, and Rapier 3D, featuring instanced kit geometry, real-time physics, six crew NPCs, and a zero-latency dual-mode UI.
- Tags: Next.js 15, React 19, Three.js, React Three Fiber, Rapier 3D, TypeScript, Zustand 5.
- Live demo: none (this site).
- Source: https://github.com/DmytroHnylytskyi/Resume/tree/main/Aetheria
- Features:
  1. 1,059 placed objects built from 45 unique Space Base models; repeated props rendered with `THREE.InstancedMesh`.
  2. Rapier 3D physics simulation with fixed 60 Hz timestep and third-person controller.
  3. Skeletal glTF character animation with smooth state transitions (Idle, Walk, Run, Jump).
  4. Zero-latency bilingual switching (UK/EN) and theme toggle (Dark/Light) via Zustand 5.

---

## 4. 3D outpost — complete map

### 4.1 Entry, loading and first frame

1. The visitor presses `3D` / “Launch 3D Experience” / the artifact's third link / the footer “See you in 3D”.
2. On desktop, a warp animation plays over the classic singularity background; on mobile the switch is immediate.
3. A black “wormhole arrival” curtain fades out over ~0.9 s while the 3D chunk downloads.
4. A loading overlay shows the AETHERIA 3D brand, a spinner, “Loading 3D World…”, the subtitle “Compiling shaders, 3D assets, and physics simulation”, a progress bar (minimum visible 12%), and the tip that the visitor can switch between 3D and the classic resume at any time.
5. The loader waits for the character and the shader warm-up, then fades out. A 15 s safety fallback releases a stalled queue.
6. The cinematic intro starts only after the world is ready, and only on the first visit (or when replayed).

### 4.2 Cinematic intro

- A camera flight over the outpost: from an establishing point above the deck, over the hub and solar field, ending behind the player at spawn.
- The DOM overlay shows the `AETHERIA` wordmark, the author's name and role, and “Press anything to skip”.
- Duration is about 4.8 s; an 8 s failsafe ends it if the frame loop stalls.
- Any key or pointer press skips it.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` skips it entirely.
- Completion is stored in `aetheria_intro_seen`; repeat visitors land directly at spawn.
- It can be replayed from the Controls guide → “Replay cinematic intro”.
- The HUD top bar is hidden during the intro.

Spawn: `[-8, 1.1, 12]`, yaw `-0.25`.

### 4.3 Controls

Desktop / keyboard and mouse:

| Input | Action |
|---|---|
| W, A, S, D or arrow keys | Move |
| Shift | Sprint |
| Space | Jump |
| Click the canvas to lock the pointer, then move the mouse | Orbit the camera 360° |
| Mouse wheel | Zoom the camera (2.2–7.0 m) |
| `E` | Interact with crew / open the dossier when the interaction pill is visible |
| `M` | Toggle the tactical map |
| `H` | Toggle the controls guide |
| `Escape` | Close the active modal, dialogue, map or guide |

Pointer lock is requested when the visitor clicks the canvas outside modals; while locked, mouse movement orbits the camera. The Controls guide labels this “RMB / LMB + Drag”, but the implemented desktop path is pointer lock. On touch devices, a right-side drag orbits the camera.

Touch / mobile:

| Input | Action |
|---|---|
| Left virtual stick | Move; pushing to the rim sprints |
| Right-side drag | Orbit the camera |
| Two-finger pinch | Zoom |
| Jump button | Jump |
| Interaction pill | Talk to the crew / open the dossier |
| Radar button | Open the tactical map |

The Controls guide has two tabs (Touch / Keyboard), lists movement, camera and actions, and includes the replay-intro button. It opens with `H` and closes with `Escape`, the X button or an outside click.

Movement constants: walk 2.6 m/s, sprint 4.6 m/s, jump impulse 5.5, fixed 60 Hz Rapier physics. If the player falls below `y = -3`, the body is reset to the spawn point.

### 4.4 HUD

Top glass bar:

- Brand: the author's name and the `Aetheria 3D` tag.
- `Resume` — switch back to the classic view.
- `About Me` — opens the Bio modal.
- `Skills` — opens the Skills modal.
- `Contact` — opens the Contacts modal.
- `Crew N/6` — opens the tactical map; becomes visibly complete when all six are met.
- `Controls` — opens the controls dropdown.
- Time-of-day slider with moon and sun caps.
- Fallback theme button on small screens.
- Audio toggle.
- EN / UA language switch.

Other HUD layers:

- A short onboarding pill for the first 7 s (or until the first input): desktop `[W, A, S, D] to move • [Space] jump • [E] interact • [H] guide`; touch `Left stick to move • Drag right to look • [E] interact`.
- A floating interaction pill when the player is within ~2.5 m of crew: desktop shows the `E` key and the action title; touch shows a sparkle icon and “Open: <title>”.
- The mini-radar at the bottom-right.
- Dialogue, modal and map layers when open.

### 4.5 Mini-radar

- Circular glass housing, about 124 px on desktop and 74 px on mobile.
- Island contour, north/east/south/west compass points, grid rings, crosshair.
- Six crew blips at their real map positions, each in its sector colour. Unmet crew are visually distinguished.
- A player pin with a direction cone that follows position and camera yaw at 60 FPS.
- Hovering a blip shows the crew member's name.
- Clicking the housing or the “Map [M]” button opens the tactical map.

### 4.6 Tactical map

- Full-screen modal with a dark backdrop.
- Title: “Aetheria Outpost Tactical Map” / “Тактична карта аванпосту Aetheria”.
- Subtitle: `Crew N/6 · materials N/6`.
- A 900×900 canvas schematic drawn from `islandScene.json` and measured model bounds: floor plates by tier, large modules, tunnels, cargo, solar field, dashed crew route, spawn marker, 10 m grid and platform frame.
- Six numbered pins at the real crew positions; the next unvisited sector pulses.
- A player pin with heading, updated live.
- “LIVE SCHEMATIC” caption and a north arrow.
- Sidebar:
  - Stats `Crew N/6` and `Materials N/6`.
  - A row per crew member with number, name, sector and status: `NEXT` / `VISITED` / `UNMET` (UK: `ДАЛІ` / `ПРОЙДЕНО` / `НЕ ЗНАЙОМІ`).
  - Hint: “Click a pin or a row to open the dossier / project. Hover a pin for its name.”
- Clicking a pin or row opens the corresponding dossier/project and closes the map.
- Close by X, `Escape` or backdrop click.
- The map shows only the six crew; there is no shuttle pin or shuttle silhouette.

### 4.7 Dialogue HUD

- Opens when the visitor presses `E` (or the interaction pill) near a crew member.
- A full-screen backdrop with an obsidian glass dialogue sheet.
- Header: profession icon, crew name, role, sector badge, close button.
- Body: the crew line typed at 2 characters every 22 ms, with a caret.
- Clicking the text, `Enter` or `Space` skips to the full line.
- Footer: “Close” and the primary action (e.g. “Open dossier”, “Stack & certifications”, “Contact Dmytro”, “Launch Forma-3D”).
- The primary action closes the dialogue, marks the corresponding material as opened and opens the modal/project.
- A “Next: <sector>” hint points to the nearest sector whose crew has not been met; when all six are met it says “Whole crew accounted for — dossier complete”.
- Close by X, `Escape`, the backdrop or “Close”.
- The sector colour is used as an accent only; all six dialogues share one frame.

### 4.8 Crew dossier

- Meeting a crew member is recorded when the dialogue opens.
- Opening a material is recorded when the primary action is pressed.
- Six materials, one per crew member: `bio`, `skills`, `contacts`, `forma`, `terrascope`, `lumina`.
- Progress is stored in `localStorage['aetheria_dossier']` and restored on reload.
- `Crew N/6` reflects meetings; `Materials N/6` reflects opened materials.
- A store action `resetDossier()` exists, but there is no visible reset button in the UI.

### 4.9 Modals

All modals share the obsidian glass panel, a coloured top accent line, a focus trap, `Escape` to close, and backdrop click to close.

**Bio modal**

- Name, role, location, KPI degree badge.
- Full bio paragraph.
- Education card: institution, faculty, specialty, degree, period, status.
- “Key Engineering Highlights”: the four summary bullets.

**Skills modal**

- Two tabs:
  - “Tech Stack”: four categories with all skill chips.
  - “Certifications”: all seven verified credentials with issuer, level, category and a Verified marker. The tab badge shows `7`.
- Close by button, backdrop or `Escape`.

**Contacts modal**

- Availability banner with a pulsing status dot.
- Kyiv timezone pill: `Kyiv (UTC+2 / UTC+3)`.
- Telegram card (primary/fast response) with `@mokydjin`, external link and copy button.
- Email card with a mailto link and copy button.
- GitHub card with the profile link.
- Copy feedback changes the icon to a check for ~2.2 s.

**Project modal**

- Same layout as the classic project modal, opened from Nova, Orion or Lyra, or from a tactical-map pin.
- Contains the preview, tagline, description, four features, stack and footer links.

### 4.10 Crew roster

| # | ID | Name (EN / UK) | Role (EN / UK) | Sector | Colour | Position | Opens |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | commander | Commander Kira / Командир Кіра | Expedition Commander / Командир експедиції | BIO-ARCHIVE / БІО-АРХІВ | `#fbbf24` gold | `[5.5, 1.4, -6.1]` | Bio modal |
| 2 | chief_engineer | Chief Engineer Vex / Головний інженер Векс | Reactor & Systems Architect / Архітектор реактора і систем | REACTOR CORE / ЯДРО РЕАКТОРА | `#c084fc` violet | `[-16.7, 4.0, -10.6]` | Skills modal |

Visit order is 1 → 6. The narrative order is bio → skills → Forma-3D → TerraScope → Lumina → contacts. The “Next” hint is based on the physically nearest unmet sector, not the fixed order.

Dialogue lines shown in-game (English, verbatim):

- **Kira:** “Welcome aboard Aetheria Outpost. I'm Commander Kira. This station is Dmytro's work — every system here, from database schemas to WebGL shaders, built on a Kyiv Polytechnic (KPI) software engineering degree and four years of full-stack practice. My archive holds his full record.”
- **Vex:** “Reactor's stable. Sixty FPS on deterministic Rapier physics, no per-frame allocations, strict TypeScript across the stack, React 19 and Next.js 15 underneath. The technical passport — stack and certifications — is on this console.”
- **Nova:** “This deck runs Forma-3D, our generative CAD in the browser: parametric splines, real-time mesh operations and instant glTF export. The demo is interactive — you can model something yourself.”
- **Orion:** “Orbital telemetry is streaming: TerraScope renders multispectral imagery as live geospatial layers — millions of coordinates, tile pyramids and vector streams in real time. The platform is open for inspection.”
- **Lyra:** “Keep clear of the beam path. Lumina is our learning platform: interactive media players, automated code checks and live student analytics. The demo is ready when you are.”
- **Tayra:** “The subspace array is locked on Kyiv and the channel is clean. Mail, Telegram and GitHub are live — send your project or offer through this uplink and it reaches Dmytro directly.”

Two of these lines contain copy that disagrees with the current project data; see §9.

### 4.11 Sectors

| reactor_core | REACTOR CORE | ЯДРО РЕАКТОРА | `#c084fc` | 8 m | `[-16.7, 4.0, -10.6]` | Chief Engineer Vex |
| generative_lab | GENERATIVE LAB | ГЕНЕРАТИВНА ЛАБОРАТОРІЯ | `#34d399` | 5 m | `[7.5, 1.0, -3.2]` | UI Architect Nova |
| orbital_gis | ORBITAL GIS | ОРБІТАЛЬНИЙ ГІС | `#60a5fa` | 8 m | `[22.5, 1.0, 24.3]` | Geodata Analyst Orion |
| lumina_optics | LUMINA OPTICS | ОПТИКА LUMINA | `#fb7185` | 8 m | `[21.8, 1.0, 15.6]` | Photonics Specialist Lyra |

Sector radii overlap in the hub; the nearest sector wins.

### 4.12 Day/night cycle

- Continuous position `0..0.999`, where `0` and `1` are midnight and `0.5` is noon.
- Period labels: Midnight, Dawn, Morning, Noon, Golden, Sunset, Dusk, Midnight (UK: Північ, Світанок, Ранок, Полудень, Золото, Захід, Сутінки).
- The slider track is a gradient sampled from the same sky colours used by the WebGL dome.
- Moon cap: cinematic flight to night (`1`). Sun cap: cinematic flight to day (`0.5`).
- The DOM theme switches at sun-elevation thresholds with hysteresis: light above `+0.06`, dark below `-0.04`.
- The position is persisted in `aetheria_time_of_day` and shared by classic and 3D.
- The cycle drives sky gradients, the sun/moon key light, lamp emissive intensity, lamp halos and ground pools, the Milky Way, star opacity and the singularity palette.
- On a first visit with no saved position, an OS-dark visitor starts at midnight; otherwise at noon.

### 4.13 Audio

- Muted by default. The toggle is in both headers.
- Enabling starts the ambient track `/audio/aetheria-ambient.mp3` (about 1.15 MB) and a procedural synth drone fallback.
- UI cues are synthesized: clicks, interaction, jump, footsteps, warp/portal.
- Audio never autoplays before a user gesture.

### 4.14 Camera, movement and physics

- Third-person orbital camera with independent yaw/pitch smoothing and collision pull-in.
- Zoom range 2.2–7.0 m; initial distance 2.8 m.
- Pointer lock on canvas click; while locked, mouse movement orbits the camera. Touch uses a right-side drag.
- Kinematic-style character velocity with momentum interpolation.
- Walk 2.6 m/s, sprint 4.6 m/s, jump impulse 5.5, gravity from Rapier.
- Rapier 3D fixed 60 Hz timestep; capsule body; terrain and prop colliders.
- Camera collision uses three rays (centre, left, right) against the physics world and pulls in near walls.
- Falling below `y = -3` resets the body to spawn.
- The store contains a legacy `cameraMode` field (`third_person` / `bird_eye`) but there is no visible control for it. Do not expect a camera-mode toggle.

### 4.15 Mobile behaviour

- Touch is detected via `ontouchstart`, `maxTouchPoints`, `pointer: coarse` or a small viewport.
- In portrait, a full-screen guard appears: “Please Rotate Your Device”, “Aetheria 3D is designed for landscape orientation with dual-thumb controls.”
  - “Fullscreen Mode” button (on iOS it shows “Fullscreen on iPhone” guidance instead).
  - “Read Vertically as Resume” button switches to the classic view.
  - iOS hint: Safari “aA” → “Hide Toolbar”, or Share → “Add to Home Screen”.
- In landscape: left joystick, right-side orbit, pinch zoom, jump button, interaction pill, radar.
- Mobile quality is chosen from GPU/cores/memory, not merely from `pointer: coarse`; a flagship phone can receive high quality with DPR up to 2.0.

### 4.16 World contents and celestial scene

Outpost:

- 1,059 placed objects from 45 unique models.
- 859 terrain plates, 31 lamps, 6 crew NPC models.
- Repeated props use `THREE.InstancedMesh`; static kit geometry is merged per model to keep draw calls low.
- Colliders are generated from measured mesh AABBs and checked by a separate collider gate.
- The scene comes from `islandScene.json`, produced by the Forma-3D map importer.

Celestial scene:

- **Planet below the platform:** radius 800, centre `(0, -920, 0)`, so its top is about 120 m below the deck. Earth-like surface with ocean, continents, mountain provinces, snow, beaches; a separate cloud sphere at radius +10; an atmosphere shell at radius ×1.012. The surface and clouds are baked once into a 36° cap texture (2048² on touch/low/medium, 4096² on high desktop) and use a small tiled detail-normal map at runtime. Clouds drift; the planet itself is static.
- **Starfield:** 700 / 1,100 / 1,400 stars by quality tier on a sphere of radius 800; varied sizes, five colour temperatures, per-star twinkle.
- **Milky Way:** a faint band with dust clumps in the sky dome, visible at night.
- **Shattered moon:** radius 32 at `(150, 62, 205)`, with 12 floating fragments and 70 debris points, plus a rim glow. No glowing crack.
- **Megastructure:** two broken orbital arcs, inner radius 54, outer 58.5, at `(0, 76, 232)`, with 16 navigation lights per arc.
- **Gravitational singularity:** about 170 m from the deck at roughly 18° above the horizon, scale 1.8, with an accretion disk and halo. It is the visual replacement for the sun/moon and remains the hero object in the northern sky.
- **Cosmic dust:** 350 / 650 / 1,000 additive points by tier, spread across the sky.
- Camera far plane 1000; shadow-camera far 200.

### 4.17 Quality tiers and performance budget

| Setting | High | Medium | Low |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shadows | Yes, 1536 desktop / 1024 touch | No | No |
| Materials | MeshStandardMaterial | MeshStandardMaterial | MeshLambertMaterial |
| Extra lights | Yes | No | No |
| DPR cap | 1.5 desktop / 2.0 touch | 1.5 | 1.0 |
| DPR floor | 0.85 desktop / 0.75 touch | 0.7 | 0.6 |
| Stars | 1,400 | 1,100 | 700 |
| Dust | 1,000 | 650 | 350 (every other frame) |
| MSAA | Fine pointer yes; coarse pointer no | Fine pointer yes; coarse pointer no | Fine pointer yes; coarse pointer no |
| Rich effects (rings, halos) | Yes | Yes | No |
| Planet bake | 4096² desktop only; 2048² touch | 2048² | 2048² |

- Tier is selected from the GPU string, hardware concurrency, device memory, DPR and handheld signals.
- `?q=low|medium|high` overrides detection at canvas mount.
- Software renderers (SwiftShader/llvmpipe) and weak Intel integrated GPUs fall back to low.
- Adaptive DPR raises/lowers resolution by small steps based on FPS; it avoids frequent swapchain reallocations.
- Physics runs at a fixed 60 Hz. The UI and camera target 60 FPS; this is a target, not a guarantee on every device.

### 4.18 Accessibility and limits of the 3D mode

- Modals and the dialogue trap focus and close on `Escape`.
- The HUD has ARIA labels and titles for its controls.
- The instructions guide is keyboard-accessible (`H`).
- The 3D canvas itself is not exposed to screen readers. The classic resume is the accessible text equivalent.
- The scene is not deep-linkable: there is no URL that opens a specific dialogue, sector or modal. Use the QA bridge (§7) or normal navigation.
- Audio is muted by default.
- The 3D world is intentionally heavy on first load (Three.js, Rapier, models); the classic view is the lightweight path.

---

## 5. Complete visitor checklist

### Classic

- [ ] Read hero, status, location, Kyiv clock, stats.
- [ ] Filter projects by a skill; clear the filter.
- [ ] Open a project modal; inspect features and links.
- [ ] Read about, education, all four skill groups, all seven certifications.
- [ ] Open a certificate's public credential.
- [ ] Change the time of day; observe the theme and sky.
- [ ] Toggle audio.
- [ ] Switch EN ↔ UA; check the URL updates.
- [ ] Print/save the CV.
- [ ] Copy the email; observe the toast.
- [ ] Enter 3D from at least one CTA.
- [ ] Use the skip link and back-to-top.

### 3D

- [ ] Watch or skip the intro; replay it from Controls.
- [ ] Move, sprint, jump, orbit and zoom.
- [ ] Meet all six crew; read all six dialogues.
- [ ] Open bio, skills, contacts and all three project modals.
- [ ] Watch the `Crew N/6` and `Materials N/6` counters.
- [ ] Reload and confirm the dossier persists.
- [ ] Open the tactical map; use a pin and a sidebar row.
- [ ] Scrub to midnight and noon; observe lamps, stars, planet and theme.
- [ ] Toggle audio.
- [ ] Switch to classic and back.
- [ ] On a phone: rotate to landscape, use the joystick, jump, orbit, pinch; try the portrait guard.

## 6. Visual language

### 6.1 Shared

- Both modes share the day/night sky palette, the warm accent `--tod-glow` (default `#ffe9b8`), glass panels, thin borders, and the same obsidian modal/dialogue family in 3D.
- The site is designed to read as one product: the classic page is the “document” view of the same universe, the 3D outpost is the “place” view.

### 6.2 Classic

- Editorial, technical, monochrome. Black or white page, high-contrast type, restrained colour.
- Space Grotesk for display; system UI for body.
- Numbered sections 01–08, eyebrow labels, large headings, thin rules, generous spacing.
- Surfaces: glass cards with 26 px radii, subtle borders, pointer spotlight on desktop.
- Project cards mimic a browser window: traffic lights, URL chrome, screenshot, “Explore project”.
- Hero: oversized name, rotating specialty, typed bio, kinetic orbital cube with nine orbit planes.
- Background: a WebGL quasar/singularity vortex behind the content, plus a sky tint and aura that follow the time of day.
- Motion: scroll reveals, sticky project scene, pointer tilt/light, typed text, rotating role — all disabled or reduced under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

### 6.3 3D

- Stylized low-poly sci-fi outpost built from KayKit Space Base modules; readable silhouettes, warm lamps, teal/violet night, strong sector colour coding.
- Multi-tier platform with a hub, upper plateau, solar field, tunnels, cargo, landing pad and industrial props.
- HUD: dark obsidian glass, thin luminous borders, small uppercase labels, sector-coloured accents.
- Celestial composition: a huge Earth-like planet below the deck, a dense starfield and Milky Way above, a shattered moon and broken orbital arcs in the southern sky, and a black hole in the northern sky.
- Lighting: one shadow-casting key light (sun by day, moon by night), cool fill and hemisphere light, additive lamp halos and ground pools at night.
- The look is deliberately “physical place first, UI second”: the HUD is compact and the scene is meant to be explored.

---

## 7. Debug and QA API

These hooks exist only when the corresponding query parameter is present. They have no cost in normal production use.

### 7.1 Activation

- `?debug` (any value): mounts the physics wireframe overlay, attaches `window.__aetheriaDebug`, and also enables the renderer probe. **The collider wireframes are visible by default**; call `window.__aetheriaDebug.showColliders(false)` before taking screenshots.
- `?probe`: enables `window.__aetheria` only (no physics overlay, no teleport).

Use `?mode=3d&debug` to land directly in the 3D world with the bridge active.

### 7.2 `window.__aetheria` — renderer probe

```js
window.__aetheria.info()
// { calls, triangles, points, lines, programs, geometries, textures, dpr }

window.__aetheria.setDpr(1)
// Fixed pixel ratio for honest measurements.

window.__aetheria.time(0.5)
// Set the day/night cycle: 0.5 = noon, 0 = midnight, 0.75 = sunset.

window.__aetheria.fly(px, py, pz, tx, ty, tz)
// Fixed QA camera. Example: fly(8, 6, 34, 0, 1, 0) matches the intro's opening view.

window.__aetheria.flyOff()
// Return control to the player camera.
```

### 7.3 `window.__aetheriaDebug` — player and physics bridge

```js
window.__aetheriaDebug.x // current player X (also .y, .z)
window.__aetheriaDebug.teleport(x, y, z)
window.__aetheriaDebug.setCamera(yaw, pitch, distance?) // radians, metres
window.__aetheriaDebug.showColliders(true)
window.__aetheriaDebug.listNear(2.2) // colliders near the player
window.__aetheriaDebug.propsNear(4)  // placed props near the player
```

### 7.4 Deterministic examples

Teleport next to Commander Kira and aim the camera west (Kira is at `x = 5.5`; the player is placed at `x = 7.5`, within the 2.5 m interaction radius):

```js
window.__aetheriaDebug.showColliders(false); // hide the QA wireframe overlay
window.__aetheriaDebug.teleport(7.5, 1.2, -6.1);
window.__aetheriaDebug.setCamera(Math.PI / 2, -0.08, 3.2);
// Wait a frame, then press E to open the dialogue.
```

Open the tactical map: press `M`, or click the “Map [M]” button.

Open a specific dossier without walking: teleport near the crew member, press `E`, then click the primary action in the dialogue. Coordinates are in §4.10–4.11.

Capture a night frame:

```js
window.__aetheria.time(0);
// Wait ~1 s for the tween; the lamps, stars and theme update.
```

Measure the scene:

```js
window.__aetheria.setDpr(1);
window.__aetheria.info();
```

The debug bridge does not expose the React store or a “open modal by id” function. The reliable path is teleport → interaction → click, or click the HUD shortcuts.

---

## 8. Visual evaluation protocol

### 8.1 Preconditions

- Use a browser with WebGL 2 and a real GPU if possible. A software renderer will fall back to low quality and will look different.
- Use a fresh profile for the first-visit intro. To skip it deliberately, set `localStorage.setItem('aetheria_intro_seen', '1')` before loading.
- To test the light theme from a deterministic state, clear `aetheria_time_of_day` or set it to `0.5`.
- Wait for the loader to finish and the intro to end or be skipped before capturing.
- If the URL uses `?debug`, call `window.__aetheriaDebug.showColliders(false)` first; otherwise yellow/coloured collider wireframes will appear in every frame.
- For the classic page, wait for hydration and the reveal animations (about 1 s) before a full-page capture.

### 8.2 Suggested viewports and URLs

| Target | Viewport | URL |
|---|---|---|
| Classic desktop | 1440×900 or 1600×900 | `/?mode=classic&lang=en` |
| Classic mobile | 390×844 | `/?mode=classic&lang=en` |
| Classic dark | 1440×900 | same, then scrub to night |
| 3D desktop high | 1600×900 | `/?mode=3d&q=high&debug&lang=en` |
| 3D mobile landscape | 844×390 | `/?mode=3d&q=medium&lang=en` |
| 3D mobile portrait guard | 390×844 | `/?mode=3d&lang=en` |
| Ukrainian | any | append `&lang=uk` |

### 8.3 Frames to capture

Classic:

1. Hero at first paint (name, role, typed bio, stats, artifact).
2. Projects section with all four cards.
3. Filtered projects state (click a skill chip).
4. About + education.
5. Skills + certifications.
6. 3D CTA + contacts.
7. Recognition + footer.
8. Project modal.
9. Print preview (`page.emulateMedia({ media: 'print' })`).
10. Night theme hero.
11. Mobile hero and mobile project card.
12. Ukrainian hero or section.

3D:

1. Loading overlay.
2. Intro title frame (if testing first visit).
3. Spawn view after landing.
4. A sector close-up with a crew member and marker.
5. Dialogue sheet.
6. Tactical map.
7. Bio modal.
8. Skills modal (both tabs).
9. Contacts modal.
10. Project modal.
11. Day frame (`time(0.5)`) and night frame (`time(0)`).
12. A wide `fly(...)` establishing frame showing the platform, planet and sky.
13. Mobile landscape HUD with joystick.
14. Mobile portrait orientation guard.
15. Ukrainian HUD/dialogue.

### 8.4 Rubric

Judge each frame against the user's acceptance bar, not against code claims.

- **First-glance readability at 25% thumbnail:** is the name/role/primary action (classic) or the platform/hero object (3D) immediately legible?
- **Hierarchy:** clear primary, secondary and tertiary elements; no competing headlines.
- **Typography:** no clipping, overflow, orphan headings, or unreadably small labels; line lengths are comfortable.
- **Contrast:** text is readable in both themes; no white-on-white or black-on-black states.
- **Consistency:** classic and 3D share the same accent, glass and border language; sector colours are used consistently across markers, map, dialogue and modals.
- **Classic composition:** numbered sections align; cards do not crowd; the hero artifact does not collide with text; project chrome and screenshots are crisp.
- **3D composition:** the platform reads as a place, not a pile of props; the planet, moon, arcs and black hole are visible in the intended directions; no empty black void where the planet should be.
- **HUD:** the top bar does not overlap the scene's focal point; the radar stays inside the viewport; the interaction pill is legible; no HUD during the intro.
- **Map:** six pins are distinct and numbered; the route is readable; the sidebar is not clipped; statuses match the dossier.
- **Modals/dialogue:** content fits, scrolls where needed, buttons remain reachable, focus is visible, `Escape` works.
- **Mobile:** landscape guard appears in portrait; joystick and jump do not overlap the radar; safe-area insets are respected.
- **Day/night:** both states are readable; lamps and windows glow at night; the planet is not washed out or flat pale blue; stars are visible.
- **Performance:** steady frame rate on the test machine; no multi-second stall after the loader; no flicker from resolution changes.
- **Accessibility:** skip link, focus outlines, ARIA labels, keyboard path through the classic page.

### 8.5 Fail conditions

- A black or empty canvas after the loader.
- Text overlapping or clipped at a supported viewport.
- The tactical map missing pins or showing the shuttle.
- A modal that cannot be closed with `Escape` or the X.
- The 3D HUD visible during the intro.
- The planet rendering as a flat pale disk (a known shader failure signature: missing `modelMatrix` in the fragment shader).
- The classic page requiring JavaScript to show its text.
- Audio autoplaying before a gesture.

---

## 9. Known caveats and stale copy

These are visible or source-level inconsistencies. The profile/project data is authoritative unless stated otherwise.

1. **Kira's line says “four years of full-stack practice”; the profile summary says “2+ years”.** Treat the profile summary as authoritative. The line is in-game copy.
2. **Nova's line describes Forma-3D as “generative CAD … parametric splines, real-time mesh operations and instant glTF export”.** The current Forma-3D feature list is surface snapping, freefly camera, real-time material customization and async scene persistence, with Scene JSON import/export. The Forma README does not advertise splines or glTF export. Treat `resumeData.ts` and the Forma repository as authoritative.
3. **“Download PDF” opens the browser print dialog**, not a generated file. The dedicated print document is what the browser prints or saves.
4. **“60 FPS” is a target.** It appears in project descriptions and crew dialogue; actual performance depends on the device and quality tier.
5. **Legacy `cameraMode` field.** The store has `third_person` / `bird_eye` and a toggle action, but no UI exposes it. There is no camera-mode switch for visitors.
6. **No welcome/mode-selection gate.** `isInitialWelcomeOpen` exists in the store for legacy guards but is always `false`. The site opens directly on the classic page.
7. **No dossier reset button.** `resetDossier()` exists in the store but is not wired to visible UI. A visitor can clear `localStorage['aetheria_dossier']` manually.
8. **3D is not screen-reader accessible.** The classic resume is the accessible equivalent.
9. **Quality and appearance depend on hardware.** Software rendering and weak GPUs fall back to low; the planet bake is 2048² there and 4096² only on high desktop.
10. **The Web Guru badge image is served from an external CDN.** If the CDN is unavailable, the badge may not render.
11. **Forma's live URL redirects** from `/` to `/en` (HTTP 307).
12. **`?mode=3d` briefly serves classic HTML** before hydration switches the mode. Automated visual tests should wait for the canvas.
13. **The 3D scene has no deep links** to a specific crew member, sector or modal. Use the QA bridge or walk.
14. **The tactical map intentionally omits the shuttle.** It is world decoration, not a route point.

---

- Original code, shaders, UI, composition and design are **source-available under PolyForm Strict 1.0.0**.
- Viewing and noncommercial evaluation are welcome.
- Redistribution, modification, derivative works and commercial use require written permission from the author.
- KayKit Space Base Bits and Character Animations are officially **CC0 1.0**: free to use, including commercially; attribution is optional. The repository's license cannot and does not restrict those assets.
- The Web Guru Awards badge belongs to Web Guru Awards and is used for the award recognition block.
- This passport is descriptive. It grants no rights to the code, assets or design; it exists so agents can understand and evaluate the public site.

## 12. Verification

- Last source review: 2026-10-22.
- Measured from the current repository: 1,059 placed objects, 45 unique models, 859 terrain plates, 31 lamps, 6 NPC models, 39 glTF + 11 GLB model files.
- The live site was checked on 2026-10-22: `/`, `/robots.txt` and `/sitemap.xml` return 200. Locally, a Next dev server serves `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt` with HTTP 200 and `text/plain`; the production deployment will expose them after the next release.
- Cross-checks: profile and project data from `src/data/resumeData.ts`; crew and sectors from `npcDialogues.ts` and `zones.ts`; controls from `ControlsGuideDropdown.tsx` and `CharacterController.tsx`; quality from `debugState.ts`; celestial constants from the 3D components.
- If a future build changes counts, copy, coordinates or controls, this file should be updated in the same commit as the change.
